title: GeoJSON Feature Total Checker: As Promised?
description: Check a GeoJSON file's feature total against what was promised with the GeoJSON Feature Total Checker — deliveries verified in seconds. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a supplier’s manifest promises 1,250 features and the delivered file totals 1,247 — three missing features found in seconds, before integration swallowed the discrepancy.
quick_answer: The GeoJSON Feature Total Checker counts the features in a FeatureCollection or single-Feature input so you can check the total against what a delivery, an export job or a manifest claims. Paste the GeoJSON and compare — the acceptance test turning ‘looks about right’ into a number.

body.t: Contracts and manifests promise feature counts. This check is the receiving dock’s scale — weigh every delivery before it enters your systems. The plain count itself lives at the
An ETL job logs ‘wrote 48,201 features’. Paste the output and verify the file agrees with the log — jobs lie most politely in their summaries.
Downloads cut mid-stream and APIs paginate silently. A total short of the source’s count is the truncation alarm.
Convert out and back, then compare totals: format round-trips that quietly drop a feature fail this check, as they should.

1,250 promised, 1,247 delivered: the likeliest stories are null-geometry features filtered by an exporter, a pagination cap at a round number minus a hiccup, or a boundary clip. The check cannot say which — it guarantees the conversation starts from a fact.
Totals can exceed the manifest too — a join that fanned out rows duplicates features wholesale. Over-delivery is also a discrepancy, and in spatial data usually the worse one.

rows: Filtered nulls or invalid geometries dropped on export
Pagination or a LIMIT clause somewhere upstream
Wrong file, empty export, or a geometry-only document
popular_table.note: The checker counts what is in the file — Features in a FeatureCollection, one for a lone Feature. What the file should contain is the manifest’s claim; the gap between them is the finding.

faq: Features — the members of a FeatureCollection’s features array, or a single Feature as one. The count is structural and total, ready to stand next to any claimed figure.
How is it different from the Feature Counter?
Same census, different job: the counter reports a number; this checker is framed for reconciliation — the number against a promise, with the discrepancy patterns interpreted.
Totals 1 — a valid delivery shape for single-object exchanges, checked as honestly as a million-feature collection.
What if the file is bare geometry?
Zero features — which against any positive promise is itself the discrepancy report: the exporter shipped geometry without its feature wrappers.
Can it find WHICH features are missing?
Counts prove existence of a gap, not identity. Diffing ids between manifest and file is the follow-up — feature id properties make it mechanical.
Yes — every array member counts, duplicates included. A total can match while duplication and omission cancel out; id-level checks catch that darker case.
No — a feature with broken coordinates still counts as a feature. Validation is a separate gate; the total is a census, not a health certificate.
